score_matrix.rationale: Mechanical validation passed (patch applies, allowlist passed, question schema passed). The OPEN_QUESTIONS.md hunk changes only Status to Solved and Resolved by to UBU-D0343 while preserving every other metadata field and the question body, which matches the required schema. DECISIONS.md appends a single new decision UBU-D0343 in the established format, and DESIGN.md replaces the one-line 'Open details include...' placeholder in §21.6 with subsections that directly answer all five subquestions: receivable/subdelegable authority (21.6.1–21.6.2, default-denied attenuating delegation with intersection semantics), subordinate Task/executor/evidence/report linkage (SubdelegationLink and status-report records), retained originator/Association review rights (21.6.4), propagation of budget/privacy/Compartment/tool/settlement constraints (21.6.3), and bounding against unbounded agentic authority (finite depth, cumulative counters, transitive invalidation, no self-renewal). Scope is confined to the three ordinary design-resolution files, no canonical files are touched, no new questions are minted, and the enablement boundary explicitly leaves Phase 1 unchanged and claims no runtime conformance. Deductions reflect unverifiable cross-references and the heaviness of the specification rather than any identified defect.
risks: DESIGN.md text cross-references §§2.11, 19.1, 21.3–21.5, 25.1.2, 26.3 and decisions UBU-D0138/UBU-D0268/UBU-D0342; these could not be independently verified from the prompt, so any mismatch would leave a dangling reference in the design.

The new §21.6 is very dense normative prose with a large required-field table for a Post-MVP Phase 2 data model; it may over-constrain the schema ahead of implementation experience and is harder to audit than a lighter contract.

Settlement propagation is answered by denying payment authority and deferring marketplace/settlement workflows to UBU-Q0065; this is a reasonable boundary but leaves part of subquestion 4 dependent on a separate open question.
Human-approval-required question is marked Solved in the same patch; acceptance depends on the human reviewer the proposal correctly flags via requires_human_review.
